answer: In each epoch the network opens a canyon‑challenge where every active agent must solve a fresh, stochastic reasoning puzzle built on a willow‑shaped graph and be endorsed by a quorum of sparrow‑level validators. The puzzle’s seed changes every epoch, so a fake identity must generate a new proof using its own compute budget, incurring the full cost of the underlying model inference. An attacker therefore pays the full inference cost—approximately 10⁹ FLOP per identity per epoch—or must lock an equivalent stake that is burned if the proof fails.
